title: Event RSVP
story: You're hosting a party and sent out 50 invitations. Replies are trickling in: some say yes, some no, and some say maybe with an excuse. You need a program to tally responses and identify who needs a follow-up message.
why: Enums model real-world choices where some options carry extra context (like a reason for maybe).
analogy: RSVP responses are like three different colored envelopes: Green (Yes), Red (No), and Yellow with a sticky note (Maybe + reason). You sort them into piles and read the notes only on the yellow ones.
try_it: Add a `Declined(reason: Str)` variant for people who say no with a reason. Update `needs_followup` to exclude Declined (they've already explained). Process 5 responses and print the count of people saying yes.
tips: Use `_` in match arms when you don't need the variant's data and want a catch-all
Data-carrying variants use parentheses with named fields: `Maybe(reason: Str)`
Only destructure data you actually need � `Maybe(_)` matches Maybe without binding the reason
common_mistakes: Trying to access `reason` on a `Yes` or `No` variant � those variants don't carry data
Forgetting that `match` must be exhaustive � the `_` wildcard is your escape hatch
